## 2026-11-26 | 32-Node ERCOT Fleet

## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday's fleet RT average of **$42.58/MWh** marks a sharp acceleration from the prior 3-day trend ($17.59 → $22.24 → $39.52), confirming a structural tightening in real-time conditions driven by reduced wind output (9.2 GW) against a 60.1 GW gross load backdrop with strong solar (31.4 GW) suppressing midday prices while evening demand pushed RT significantly higher. **17 spike nodes** (RT >$100/MWh) versus zero just four days ago signals a clear volatility regime shift, and the fleet captured peak RT of **$359.78/MWh** — meaningful upside for any asset dispatched in real-time during those hours. The simultaneous presence of **8 negative-price nodes** alongside 17 spike nodes underscores extreme intra-fleet price dispersion driven by transmission congestion, particularly along the BRUNI and NLARSW-PILONCIL corridors in South/West Texas. **HAMI_BESS_RN** was the standout node of the day, posting a DART of +$47.77/MWh (DA premium over RT), a 5-day avg DART of +$15.36, and an MCC benefit of +$113/MWh — confirming that DA commitment at this node was richly rewarded. Nodes in the LFSTH/DIBOL/FTDUNCAN cluster showed the flattest DART spreads (RT closely tracking DA), suggesting limited directional edge and reinforcing their NEUTRAL Sharpe classification.

## 4. WEATHER & LOAD OUTLOOK

**Today (11/26):** Cold morning lows (27–45°F across the fleet footprint) with highs in the mid-50s to mid-60s — a classic November shoulder day with modest heating load and significant solar generation potential midday. Lubbock and Wichita Falls touching 27°F at night will drive morning RT spikes in West/North Texas zones; watch for repeat overnight/early-morning RT premiums consistent with yesterday's HE01–HE03 constraint binding pattern.

**11/27–11/28 (Warming trend):** Highs recovering to 67–79°F across the state by Friday represents a meaningful load reduction from space heating. Solar output should remain robust under clear skies (precip <10% most locations), risking midday negative prices at solar-exposed West Texas nodes (MV_VALV4, FALFUR, POTEETS already posting negative RT yesterday). This warm-up will likely compress fleet RT averages back toward the $20–$30 range seen earlier this week unless wind generation drops sharply.

**11/29–12/02 (Rain risk builds):** Precipitation probability climbs materially across coastal and Central Texas by December 1–2 (Austin 20–21%, Houston 23%, Corpus 23%, Waco 24%), which will suppress solar output and potentially tighten RT. If cloud cover aligns with the 60–75°F temperature band, net load could increase moderately, supporting a mild RT price recovery. Wind uncertainty remains the key swing variable — with 9.2 GW yesterday being below seasonal norms, any further wind reduction on the warm days could keep RT elevated despite lower load.

**Dispatch implication:** Today favors overnight DA commitment to capture HE01–HE04 congestion premium, while midday hours (HE10–HE16) carry negative-price risk at solar-exposed nodes — do not commit midday capacity at FALFUR, MV_VALV4, or POTEETS in DA unless hedging a negative price.
